title: Store delivery receipts in machine-local ledger, never blocking deliveries
context: No observability into which memory records actually reach agents; can't identify compaction candidates. Prior incident (2026-08-09) leaked strategy records to public store, caught only by release sweep. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Create separate `.hunch-cache/served.db` for append-only delivery telemetry outside the reindex-rebuilt store. Record every pre-edit injection and subagent grounding. Swallow all errors on write/read — a lost receipt is noise; a blocked delivery is a broken product. Add `hunch served` command to surface most-delivered and never-delivered records.
consequences: Enables identification of records that never reached any agent (compaction start points)
Per-machine observed telemetry separate from shared store eliminates derivation/rebuild issues
Adds one-line warning when writing to public store while private overlay exists (leak prevention)
Records distinguish full 'served' events from delta 'refreshed' (still-current) updates
alternatives_rejected: Store in main reindex-rebuilt SQLite index — derived layer is dropped/rebuilt and state lost
Block delivery on receipt recording failure — product reliability > telemetry accuracy
Derive delivery state from index — cannot reconstruct observed telemetry from static store
